name: Syrup
description: Any sweetening syrup made by dissolving sugar, honey or another sweetener in water, plain or flavoured. The parent of the house syrups a bar preps.

name: Shrub
description: A drinking vinegar: fruit macerated with sugar and then sharpened with vinegar. Used in small measures to add acidity and fruit to cocktails and sodas.

name: Sherbet
description: A citrus cordial made from oleo saccharum (peel oils pulled out with sugar) dissolved in the fruit's own juice. The traditional sour and sweet base of punch.

name: Demerara Sugar
description: Coarse, golden-brown raw cane sugar with a light molasses flavour. Used for rich syrups in stirred whiskey and rum drinks.

name: Gum Arabic
description: Dried sap of the acacia tree, sold as powder or crystals. Dissolved into sugar syrup to make gomme, it adds a silky weight to stirred drinks.

name: Star Anise
description: Star-shaped dried fruit of a Chinese evergreen tree with a strong liquorice flavour. Used whole in spiced syrups, chai and as a garnish.

name: Allspice
description: Dried berry of the Jamaican pimento tree, tasting of clove, cinnamon and nutmeg together. Used whole or ground in tiki syrups, falernum and winter batters.

name: Pomegranate Juice
description: Tart, deep red juice pressed from pomegranate seeds. The base of real grenadine; use unsweetened, pure juice.

name: Grapefruit Peel
description: The outer peel of grapefruit, taken with as little white pith as possible. Its oils flavour sherbets, oleo saccharum and cordials.

name: Apple Cider Vinegar
description: Vinegar fermented from apple cider, about 5 percent acidity, with a soft fruity edge. The usual vinegar for shrubs.

name: Hot Sauce
description: Bottled chilli and vinegar sauce, such as a Louisiana or Mexican style. Dashed into Bloody Marys, Micheladas and sangrita for heat.

name: Cinchona Bark
description: Dried bark of the South American cinchona tree, the natural source of quinine and the bitter note in tonic. Buy cut bark rather than powder so it can be filtered out fully.

name: Butterfly Pea Flower
description: Dried blue flowers of Clitoria ternatea from Southeast Asia. They tint liquids deep blue and turn purple to pink when acid such as citrus is added.

name: Soy Lecithin
description: A powdered emulsifier extracted from soybeans. A small amount blended into a thin liquid lets it hold a light, stable foam known as an air.

name: Rice
description: Long-grain white rice. Soaked, blended and strained, it gives horchata its milky body; it is also used in rice orgeats and syrups.

name: Bacon Fat
description: Fat rendered from cooking smoked bacon, strained and kept warm and liquid. Used to fat wash bourbon and other spirits with a smoky, savoury flavour.

name: Simple Syrup
description: Equal parts white sugar and water by weight. The standard bar sweetener for sours, highballs and most shaken drinks.

steps.body: Weigh the sugar and the water into a clean container. Use equal weights.
Stir or blend until the sugar has fully dissolved and the syrup is clear. Hot water speeds this up; do not boil or the ratio will drift.
Cool, bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge.

name: Rich Simple Syrup
description: Two parts white sugar to one part water by weight. Sweeter and thicker than 1:1 syrup, so it adds less dilution and keeps longer.

steps.body: Combine the sugar and water in a pan over low heat.
Stir until every crystal has dissolved and the syrup is clear. Take it off the heat before it simmers.
Cool, bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge.

name: Demerara Syrup
description: Equal parts demerara sugar and water by weight. Adds a light toffee and molasses note to rum, whiskey and coffee drinks.

steps.body: Combine the demerara sugar and hot water in a pan or heatproof container.
Stir over low heat until fully dissolved. The large crystals take longer than white sugar.
Cool, bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge.

name: Rich Demerara Syrup
description: Two parts demerara sugar to one part water by weight. The usual sweetener for an Old Fashioned and other stirred drinks, measured by the barspoon.

steps.body: Combine the demerara sugar and water in a pan over low heat.
Stir until completely dissolved, without letting it boil.
Cool, bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge.

name: Gomme Syrup
description: Rich sugar syrup thickened with gum arabic. It gives stirred drinks and sours a smooth, silky texture and was the standard bar syrup of the 1800s.

recipe.note: 150 ml to bloom the gum, 300 ml for the syrup

steps.body: Stir the gum arabic into 150 ml of warm water. Cover and leave until it has fully hydrated into a thick, sticky paste, stirring now and then.
Heat the sugar with the remaining 300 ml of water over low heat, stirring until dissolved.
Add the gum mixture and stir over low heat until smooth. Do not boil. Skim any foam from the surface.
Strain through a fine sieve, cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Brown Sugar Syrup
description: Equal parts soft brown sugar and water by weight. Rounder and more caramel flavoured than white syrup; used in coffee drinks and whiskey sours.

steps.body: Combine the brown sugar and hot water.
Stir until fully dissolved, warming gently if needed.
Cool, bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge.

name: Muscovado Syrup
description: Equal parts dark muscovado sugar and water by weight. Deep molasses, liquorice and dried fruit notes that suit aged rum and whisky drinks.

steps.body: Break up any lumps in the muscovado, then combine with the hot water.
Stir over low heat until fully dissolved.
Strain through a fine sieve to catch undissolved lumps, cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Cane Syrup
description: Two parts raw, unbleached cane sugar to one part water by weight. A rich syrup with a faint grassy cane flavour, used in daiquiris and Ti' Punch.

steps.body: Combine the cane sugar and water in a pan over low heat.
Stir until completely dissolved, without boiling.
Cool, bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge.

name: Honey Syrup
description: Two parts honey loosened with one part warm water by weight so it pours and mixes cold. Used in the Bee's Knees, Gold Rush and Brown Derby.

steps.body: Weigh the honey into a container and add the warm water.
Stir until the honey has fully blended into the water. Do not boil; heat drives off the honey's aroma.
Cool, bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge.

name: Honey Syrup (1:1)
description: Equal parts honey and warm water by weight. A lighter honey syrup that can replace simple syrup measure for measure.

steps.body: Weigh equal amounts of honey and warm water into a container.
Stir until fully blended. Do not boil.
Cool, bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge. The extra water means it keeps for less time than 2:1 honey syrup.

name: Honey-Ginger Syrup
description: Honey syrup simmered and steeped with fresh ginger. The sweet and spicy base of the Penicillin.

steps.body: Combine the honey, water and sliced ginger in a pan and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer gently.
Take off the heat, cover and leave to steep in the fridge overnight.
Strain out the ginger, pressing lightly, then bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Agave Syrup Mix
description: Two parts agave syrup thinned with one part water so it pours and blends easily when cold. The sweetener for a Tommy's Margarita.

steps.body: Measure the agave syrup and warm water into a container.
Stir or shake until evenly mixed.
Bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge.

name: Maple Syrup Mix
description: Two parts pure maple syrup thinned with one part water so it measures and mixes easily in cold drinks. Used in whiskey sours and autumn cocktails.

steps.body: Measure the maple syrup and water into a container.
Stir or shake until evenly mixed.
Bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge. Diluted maple spoils faster than the pure syrup.

name: Ginger Syrup
description: Fresh ginger juice sweetened with an equal weight of sugar, made without heat to keep its bite. Used in Mules, Bucks and the Penicillin.

recipe.note: washed, juiced and fine strained, about 500 ml juice
equal to the weight of the juice

steps.body: Wash the ginger (no need to peel), juice it and strain the juice through a fine sieve.
Weigh the juice and add the same weight of sugar.
Blend or stir without heat until the sugar has fully dissolved.
Bottle and keep in the fridge. Shake before use; the heat fades after about two weeks.

name: Cinnamon Syrup
description: Simple syrup infused with cinnamon sticks. A tiki staple, used in the Zombie, Jet Pilot and Don's Mix, and in winter whiskey drinks.

steps.body: Bring the water and broken cinnamon sticks to a boil, then simmer gently with the lid on.
Take off the heat, add the sugar and stir until dissolved.
Cover and leave to steep.
Strain through a fine sieve, bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Vanilla Syrup
description: Simple syrup infused with split vanilla pods. Used in tiki drinks, the Porn Star Martini and coffee cocktails.

recipe.note: pods, split lengthways and seeds scraped

steps.body: Combine the sugar, water, vanilla seeds and pods in a pan.
Warm over low heat, stirring, until the sugar has dissolved. Do not boil.
Cover and leave to steep as it cools.
Strain out the pods, bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Raspberry Syrup
description: Fresh raspberries macerated with sugar and strained into a bright red syrup. Called for in the Clover Club and many classic punches and fizzes.

steps.body: Lightly crush the raspberries with the sugar and leave until the juices run.
Add the hot water and stir until all the sugar has dissolved.
Strain through a fine sieve or cloth. Let it drip rather than pressing hard, which makes the syrup cloudy.
Bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Strawberry Syrup
description: Ripe strawberries macerated with sugar and strained into a red fruit syrup. Used in daiquiris, spritzes and sodas.

steps.body: Toss the sliced strawberries with the sugar and leave until the juices run.
Add the hot water and stir until all the sugar has dissolved.
Strain through a fine sieve or cloth without pressing hard.
Bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Pineapple Syrup
description: Fresh pineapple steeped in simple syrup for a day and strained. A classic 19th century syrup used in the Pisco Punch and East India Cocktail.

recipe.note: ripe, peeled and cut into chunks

steps.body: Stir the sugar into the water until dissolved to make a simple syrup.
Pour the syrup over the pineapple chunks, cover and steep in the fridge.
Strain, pressing the fruit gently to release the syrup.
Bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Passion Fruit Syrup
description: Unsweetened passion fruit purée blended with rich sugar syrup. Tart and tropical; used in the Hurricane, Porn Star Martini and tiki drinks.

steps.body: Heat the sugar and water gently, stirring, until dissolved. Leave to cool.
Stir the cooled syrup into the passion fruit purée until even.
Bottle and keep in the fridge. Shake before use.

name: Grenadine
description: Pomegranate juice and sugar with a little pomegranate molasses and orange flower water. Tart, red and fruity; used in the Jack Rose and Tequila Sunrise.

steps.body: Warm the pomegranate juice over low heat until just hot. Do not boil, which dulls the fresh flavour.
Add the sugar and stir until dissolved.
Take off the heat, stir in the pomegranate molasses and orange flower water and leave to cool.
Bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Orgeat
description: Almond syrup made from fresh almond milk and sugar, scented with orange flower water. Essential to the Mai Tai, Japanese Cocktail and Army and Navy.
storage: Fridge, sealed bottle, shake before use

steps.body: Blend the toasted almonds with the hot water until finely ground.
Leave the almond mixture to steep.
Strain through a nut milk bag or cloth, squeezing out all the almond milk. You should have about 500 ml.
Stir the sugar into the almond milk over very low heat until dissolved. Do not boil.
Cool, stir in the orange flower water, bottle and keep in the fridge. It separates naturally; shake before use.

name: Falernum Syrup
description: A non-alcoholic version of the Barbadian lime, ginger, clove and almond syrup. Use in place of falernum liqueur in Corn 'n' Oil, Zombies and swizzles.

recipe.note: from about 8 limes, no white pith

steps.body: Simmer the water with the ginger, almonds, cloves and allspice, covered.
Take off the heat, add the sugar and stir until dissolved.
Add the lime zest, cover and steep as it cools.
Strain through a fine sieve and cloth, bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Don's Mix
description: Donn Beach's blend of two parts grapefruit juice to one part cinnamon syrup. The signature flavour of the Zombie and Donga Punch.

steps.body: Juice the grapefruit and fine strain it.
Combine the juice with the cinnamon syrup and stir.
Bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge. Shake before use.

name: Don's Spices No. 2
description: Donn Beach's secret tiki mix, decoded as equal parts vanilla syrup and allspice dram. Used in the Nui Nui and other Don the Beachcomber drinks.

steps.body: Measure equal parts vanilla syrup and allspice dram into a bottle.
Shake to combine, label with the date and keep in the fridge.

name: Fassionola
description: A red tropical fruit syrup from the early tiki era, built on passion fruit with strawberry, raspberry and hibiscus. Used in the Hurricane and Cobra's Fang.

steps.body: Heat the water and sugar, stirring, until dissolved.
Add the strawberries, raspberries and hibiscus and simmer very gently.
Take off the heat, cover and steep as it cools.
Strain through a fine sieve without pressing hard, then stir in the passion fruit purée.
Bottle and keep in the fridge. Shake before use.

name: Mint Syrup
description: Blanched mint leaves blended into cold simple syrup and strained. Bright green and fresh; used in juleps, Southsides and sodas.
storage: Fridge, sealed bottle, away from light

steps.body: Blanch the mint leaves in boiling water, then move them straight into iced water. This sets the green colour.
Squeeze the leaves dry and blend with the cold simple syrup until smooth.
Strain through a fine cloth or coffee filter.
Bottle and keep in the fridge. The colour and freshness fade after about a week.

name: Lavender Syrup
description: Simple syrup steeped with dried culinary lavender. Floral and lightly herbal; used in gin sours, spritzes and lemonades.

steps.body: Heat the water and sugar, stirring, until dissolved and just simmering.
Take off the heat, stir in the lavender, cover and steep. Longer steeping turns it soapy.
Strain through a fine sieve, cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Rosemary Syrup
description: Simple syrup steeped with fresh rosemary. Piney and savoury; pairs with gin, grapefruit and whiskey sours.

steps.body: Heat the water and sugar, stirring, until dissolved and just simmering.
Take off the heat, add the rosemary, cover and steep.
Strain, cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Thyme Syrup
description: Simple syrup steeped with fresh thyme. Gently herbal and earthy; works with gin, lemon, honey and stone fruit.

steps.body: Heat the water and sugar, stirring, until dissolved and just simmering.
Take off the heat, add the thyme, cover and steep.
Strain, cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Basil Syrup
description: Blanched basil leaves blended into cold simple syrup and strained. Vivid green with a sweet, peppery aroma; used in Gin Basil Smash style drinks.
storage: Fridge, sealed bottle, away from light

steps.body: Blanch the basil leaves in boiling water, then move them straight into iced water to keep them green.
Squeeze the leaves dry and blend with the cold simple syrup until smooth.
Strain through a fine cloth or coffee filter.
Bottle and keep in the fridge. Use within a week, before the colour dulls.

name: Earl Grey Syrup
description: Strong Earl Grey tea sweetened with an equal weight of sugar. Adds bergamot and gentle tannin to gin sours, punches and highballs.

steps.body: Pour the hot water over the tea and steep. Do not go much longer or the syrup turns bitter.
Strain out the tea without squeezing the leaves.
Stir the sugar into the hot tea until dissolved.
Cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Chamomile Syrup
description: Chamomile tea sweetened with an equal weight of sugar. Soft apple and honey notes; pairs with whisky, gin, pear and lemon.

steps.body: Pour the hot water over the chamomile flowers, cover and steep.
Strain through a fine sieve.
Stir the sugar into the warm tea until dissolved.
Cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Hibiscus Syrup
description: Dried hibiscus flowers steeped in hot water and sweetened. Deep red, tart and cranberry-like; used in margaritas, spritzes and agua de jamaica.

steps.body: Pour the hot water over the dried hibiscus, cover and steep.
Strain through a fine sieve, pressing the flowers lightly.
Stir the sugar into the warm liquid until dissolved.
Cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Jalapeño Syrup
description: Simple syrup steeped with sliced fresh jalapeño. Adds green chilli flavour and steady heat to margaritas and palomas.

recipe.note: sliced, seeds left in for more heat

steps.body: Heat the water and sugar, stirring, until dissolved and just simmering.
Take off the heat, add the sliced jalapeño and steep. Taste after 10 minutes and strain earlier if it is hot enough.
Strain, cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Coconut Syrup
description: Full-fat coconut milk sweetened with an equal weight of sugar. Creamy and lighter than tinned cream of coconut; used in tiki drinks and swizzles.
storage: Fridge, sealed bottle, shake before use

steps.body: Shake the tin well, then combine the coconut milk, sugar and salt in a pan.
Warm over low heat, stirring, until the sugar has dissolved. Do not boil or the milk can split.
Cool, bottle and keep in the fridge. The fat sets when cold; warm the bottle briefly and shake before use.

name: Banana Syrup
description: Ripe bananas steeped in sugar syrup and strained. Gives natural banana flavour to daiquiris, Old Fashioneds and tiki drinks.

steps.body: Stir the sugar into the hot water until dissolved.
Add the sliced banana, cover and steep in the fridge.
Strain through a fine sieve and let it drip. Do not press the fruit, which makes the syrup cloudy and starchy.
Bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Coffee Syrup
description: Strong brewed coffee sweetened with an equal weight of sugar. Used in Espresso Martinis, coffee Old Fashioneds and non-alcoholic serves.

steps.body: Brew the coffee strong and measure it while hot.
Stir in the sugar until fully dissolved.
Cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Chai Syrup
description: Black tea and whole chai spices (cinnamon, cardamom, clove, ginger, pepper) simmered and sweetened. Used in whisky, rum and coffee drinks.

steps.body: Simmer the water with all the spices and the ginger, covered.
Take off the heat, add the black tea and steep.
Strain through a fine sieve.
Stir the sugar into the hot liquid until dissolved, then cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Spiced Syrup
description: Simple syrup simmered with cinnamon, clove, allspice, star anise and orange peel. A warm baking spice note for winter drinks, punches and mulled serves.

steps.body: Simmer the water with the spices and orange peel, covered.
Take off the heat, add the sugar and stir until dissolved.
Cover and steep as it cools.
Strain through a fine sieve, bottle and keep in the fridge.

photo_query: whole spices cinnamon cloves star anise

name: Pandan Syrup
description: Simple syrup infused with pandan leaf. Grassy, nutty and vanilla-like; common in Southeast Asian style drinks with rum and coconut.

recipe.note: about 8 fresh or frozen leaves, chopped

steps.body: Heat the water and sugar, stirring, until dissolved.
Add the chopped pandan leaves and simmer gently.
Take off the heat, cover and steep.
Strain through a fine sieve, cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Lemongrass Syrup
description: Simple syrup infused with bruised lemongrass. Citrusy and lightly gingery; pairs with gin, vodka, coconut and lime.

steps.body: Heat the water and sugar, stirring, until dissolved.
Add the bruised, chopped lemongrass and simmer gently.
Take off the heat, cover and steep.
Strain through a fine sieve, cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Cucumber Syrup
description: Fresh cucumber juice sweetened with sugar, made cold to keep its green, clean flavour. Used in gin coolers, gimlets and sodas.

recipe.note: juiced and fine strained, about 500 ml juice
equal to the weight of the juice

steps.body: Juice the cucumber with the skin on and strain through a fine sieve or cloth.
Weigh the juice and add the same weight of sugar.
Stir or blend without heat until the sugar has dissolved.
Bottle and keep in the fridge. Use within four days; the fresh flavour fades quickly.

name: Peach Syrup
description: Ripe peaches gently simmered in sugar syrup and strained. Used in Bellini style drinks, iced tea, bourbon smashes and sodas.

recipe.note: ripe, stoned and sliced, skin on

steps.body: Heat the water and sugar, stirring, until dissolved.
Add the sliced peaches and simmer very gently until soft.
Take off the heat, cover and steep as it cools.
Strain through a fine sieve, pressing lightly, then bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Rhubarb Syrup
description: Chopped rhubarb simmered with sugar and water, then strained to a pink, tart syrup. Used in spritzes, gin sours and sodas.

steps.body: Trim away all the leaves (they are not edible) and chop the stalks.
Combine the rhubarb, sugar and water and simmer gently until the rhubarb is soft and has given up its colour.
Strain through a fine sieve and let it drip without pressing, to keep the syrup clear.
Cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Beetroot Syrup
description: Fresh beetroot juice sweetened with an equal weight of sugar. Earthy, sweet and deep purple; used with gin, mezcal and ginger.

recipe.note: raw, peeled and juiced, about 500 ml juice
equal to the weight of the juice

steps.body: Peel and juice the raw beetroot, then strain the juice through a fine sieve.
Weigh the juice and add the same weight of sugar.
Warm gently, stirring, just until the sugar has dissolved.
Cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Tonic Syrup
description: A bittersweet concentrate of cinchona bark, citrus peel, lemongrass and citric acid. Mix about 1 part syrup to 4 parts soda water for house tonic.

steps.body: Weigh the cinchona bark exactly; do not add extra. Simmer the water, bark, lemongrass, citrus peels and allspice, covered.
Cool, then strain through a fine sieve to remove the solids.
Filter again through a paper coffee filter until the liquid is clear and free of all bark particles. This step matters: no bark should reach the glass.
Stir in the sugar, citric acid and salt until dissolved, warming gently if needed.
Bottle and keep in the fridge. Serve 25 ml syrup to 100 ml soda water and do not exceed that strength.

name: Lime Cordial
description: Fresh lime juice and sugar steeped with lime peel for a day. A fresh house version of bottled lime cordial, used in the Gimlet.

recipe.note: from the limes before juicing, no white pith

steps.body: Peel the limes thinly before juicing them, avoiding the white pith.
Stir the sugar into the lime juice, without heat, until fully dissolved.
Add the peels, cover and steep in the fridge.
Strain out the peels, bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Oleo Saccharum
description: Lemon peels rested in sugar until their oils dissolve it into a fragrant syrup. The aromatic base of classic punch, and the first step of a sherbet.

recipe.note: from about 8 lemons, no white pith

steps.body: Peel the lemons with a vegetable peeler, taking as little white pith as possible.
Toss the peels with the sugar and muddle firmly to bruise them.
Cover (or vacuum seal) and rest at room temperature until the sugar has turned into a wet, oily syrup. Stir once or twice.
Strain off the peels, pressing to collect all the syrup. Dissolve any remaining sugar with a splash of lemon juice or hot water if needed.

name: Lemon Sherbet
description: Lemon oleo saccharum dissolved in an equal measure of fresh lemon juice. A sweet and sour punch base with the full aroma of the peel.

recipe.note: from the lemons before juicing, no white pith

steps.body: Muddle the lemon peels with the sugar, cover and rest until the sugar is wet and oily.
Add the lemon juice and stir until all the sugar has dissolved.
Strain out the peels, pressing them well.
Bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Grapefruit Sherbet
description: Grapefruit oleo saccharum dissolved in fresh grapefruit juice. Bittersweet and aromatic; used in punches, Palomas and highballs.

recipe.note: from the grapefruit before juicing, no white pith

steps.body: Muddle the grapefruit peels with the sugar, cover and rest until the sugar is wet and oily.
Add the grapefruit juice and stir until all the sugar has dissolved.
Strain out the peels, pressing them well.
Bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Elderflower Cordial
description: Fresh elderflower heads steeped for a day in sugar syrup with lemon and citric acid. A floral British cordial for spritzes, gin drinks and sodas.

recipe.note: fresh flower heads, shaken clean, thick stalks trimmed
unwaxed, zest pared and fruit sliced

steps.body: Pour the boiling water over the sugar in a large clean bowl or pan and stir until dissolved. Leave to cool until warm.
Add the lemon zest and slices, the citric acid and the elderflower heads. Stir, cover and steep somewhere cool.
Strain through a scalded muslin cloth.
Pour into sterilised bottles, seal and keep in the fridge. Freeze in tubs to keep it longer.

name: Passion Fruit Cordial
description: Passion fruit purée with sugar, water and a little citric acid. Sharper and lighter than passion fruit syrup; used in highballs, spritzes and sours.

steps.body: Stir the sugar and citric acid into the hot water until dissolved.
Leave to cool, then stir in the passion fruit purée.
Fine strain if you want it clear of pulp, bottle and keep in the fridge. Shake before use.

name: Raspberry Cordial
description: Raspberries macerated with sugar, thinned with water and sharpened with citric acid. A tart red cordial for spritzes, gin drinks and sodas.

steps.body: Crush the raspberries with the sugar and leave until the juices run.
Add the hot water and citric acid and stir until everything has dissolved.
Strain through a fine sieve or cloth without pressing hard.
Bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Ginger Cordial
description: Fresh ginger simmered in water, then sweetened and sharpened with lemon juice. Milder than raw ginger syrup; used in highballs and non-alcoholic serves.

recipe.note: washed and thinly sliced or grated

steps.body: Simmer the ginger in the water, covered.
Strain through a fine sieve, pressing the ginger firmly.
Stir the sugar into the hot liquid until dissolved, then leave to cool.
Stir in the lemon juice, bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Super Lime Juice
description: Lime peel oils extracted with citric and malic acid, blended with water and topped with the fruit's juice. Stretches a few limes into a stable lime juice substitute.

recipe.note: from about 8 limes, no white pith

storage: Fridge, sealed bottle, shake before use

steps.body: Weigh the lime peels. The recipe scales from them: 0.66 g citric acid, 0.33 g malic acid and 16.6 ml water per gram of peel.
Toss the peels with both acids in a container, cover and rest until a slick of oily liquid has formed.
Add the water and blend with a stick blender until the peels are finely chopped.
Strain through a fine cloth or superbag, squeezing it out.
Juice the peeled limes, add the juice, bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Super Lemon Juice
description: Lemon peel oils extracted with citric acid, blended with water and topped with the fruit's juice. A longer lasting, low waste stand-in for fresh lemon juice.

recipe.note: from about 6 lemons, no white pith

storage: Fridge, sealed bottle, shake before use

steps.body: Weigh the lemon peels. The recipe scales from them: 1 g citric acid and 16.6 ml water per gram of peel.
Toss the peels with the citric acid in a container, cover and rest until a slick of oily liquid has formed.
Add the water and blend with a stick blender until the peels are finely chopped.
Strain through a fine cloth or superbag, squeezing it out.
Juice the peeled lemons, add the juice, bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Acid-Adjusted Orange Juice
description: Fresh orange juice with citric and malic acid added to bring it up to the sourness of lime juice. Lets orange stand in for lemon or lime in a sour.

steps.body: Juice the oranges and fine strain the juice.
Weigh the acids accurately and add them to the juice.
Stir or shake until the powders have fully dissolved.
Bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge. Best on the day it is made.

name: Citric Acid Solution (10%)
description: Ten percent citric acid powder dissolved in water by weight. Adds clean, lemon-like sourness by the dash or millilitre without adding juice or cloudiness.

steps.body: Weigh the citric acid and the water accurately (900 ml of water weighs 900 g).
Stir or shake until the powder has completely dissolved and the liquid is clear.
Bottle and label clearly with the name, strength and date.

name: Lime Acid
description: A clear solution of 4 percent citric and 2 percent malic acid that matches the sourness of lime juice. Used to acidify stirred or clarified drinks.

steps.body: Weigh the water and both acids accurately.
Stir or shake until the powders have completely dissolved and the liquid is clear.
Bottle and label clearly with the name and date. Use measure for measure where a recipe needs the acidity of lime juice.

name: Lactic Acid Solution (10%)
description: Ten percent lactic acid in water by weight. Gives a soft, creamy, yoghurt-like sourness; used by the dash to round out clarified and stirred drinks.

recipe.note: food grade powder; if using 80% liquid, use 125 g and 875 ml water

steps.body: Weigh the lactic acid and the water accurately.
Stir or shake until completely dissolved and clear.
Bottle and label clearly with the name, strength and date.

name: Champagne Acid
description: A solution of 3 percent tartaric and 3 percent lactic acid, the main acids in Champagne. Adds a dry, wine-like brightness to stirred and carbonated drinks.

steps.body: Weigh the water and both acids accurately.
Stir or shake until the powders have completely dissolved and the liquid is clear.
Bottle and label clearly with the name and date.

name: Raspberry Shrub
description: Raspberries macerated with sugar, strained and mixed with cider vinegar. A sweet and sour drinking vinegar for highballs, spritzes and non-alcoholic serves.

steps.body: Crush the raspberries with the sugar, cover and rest in the fridge until the sugar has drawn out a thick syrup.
Strain through a fine sieve, pressing the fruit and scraping in any undissolved sugar.
Add the vinegar and stir or shake until all the sugar has dissolved.
Bottle and keep in the fridge. The flavour mellows and improves after a few days.

name: Pineapple Shrub
description: Fresh pineapple macerated with sugar, strained and mixed with cider vinegar. Tangy and tropical; pairs with rum, tequila and soda.

recipe.note: ripe, peeled and cut into small chunks

steps.body: Toss the pineapple with the sugar, cover and rest in the fridge until the sugar has drawn out a thick syrup.
Strain through a fine sieve, pressing the fruit and scraping in any undissolved sugar.
Add the vinegar and stir or shake until all the sugar has dissolved.
Bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Strawberry Shrub
description: Strawberries macerated with sugar, strained and mixed with white wine vinegar. Bright and jammy with a sharp finish; good with gin, tequila and soda.

steps.body: Toss the strawberries with the sugar, cover and rest in the fridge until the sugar has drawn out a thick syrup.
Strain through a fine sieve, pressing the fruit and scraping in any undissolved sugar.
Add the vinegar and stir or shake until all the sugar has dissolved.
Bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Bloody Mary Mix
description: Tomato juice seasoned with lemon, Worcestershire sauce, hot sauce, horseradish, celery salt and pepper. Pour about 120 ml over a measure of vodka.
storage: Fridge, sealed bottle, shake before use

steps.body: Combine all the ingredients in a jug or large container.
Stir well, taste and adjust the heat and seasoning.
Rest in the fridge so the flavours come together.
Bottle and keep in the fridge. Shake before each use.

name: Sangrita
description: A Mexican sipping chaser for tequila made from tomato, orange and lime juice with grenadine, hot sauce and salt. Served neat alongside the spirit.
storage: Fridge, sealed bottle, shake before use

steps.body: Juice and fine strain the orange and lime.
Combine everything in a jug and stir until the salt has dissolved.
Taste and adjust the heat, salt and sweetness. It should be tart, savoury and lightly spicy.
Bottle, chill well and keep in the fridge.

name: Michelada Mix
description: A savoury seasoning of lime juice, Worcestershire sauce, hot sauce and soy sauce. Add about 30 ml to a salt-rimmed glass and top with cold lager.
storage: Fridge, sealed bottle, shake before use

steps.body: Juice and fine strain the limes.
Combine all the ingredients and stir well.
Bottle and keep in the fridge. Shake before each use.

name: Saline Solution (20%)
description: Twenty percent salt dissolved in water by weight. A few drops lift flavour and soften bitterness in cocktails without making them taste salty.

recipe.note: fine sea salt or kosher salt, not iodised

storage: Room temperature, dropper or dasher bottle

steps.body: Weigh the salt and the warm water.
Stir or shake until the salt has completely dissolved and the liquid is clear.
Decant into a dropper or dasher bottle and label with the strength and date.

name: Saline Solution (10%)
description: Ten percent salt dissolved in water by weight. A gentler saline that is easier to dose by the dash in batches and single drinks.

recipe.note: fine sea salt or kosher salt, not iodised

storage: Room temperature, dropper or dasher bottle

steps.body: Weigh the salt and the warm water.
Stir or shake until the salt has completely dissolved and the liquid is clear.
Decant into a dropper or dasher bottle and label with the strength and date.

name: Chilli Tincture
description: Dried chillies steeped in vodka until fiercely hot. Dosed by the drop or dash to add heat to a drink without changing its flavour or balance.

recipe.note: dried hot chillies such as arbol or bird's eye, roughly chopped

storage: Room temperature, dropper bottle, labelled hot

steps.body: Wearing gloves, roughly chop the dried chillies and put them in a clean jar with the vodka.
Seal and infuse at room temperature, shaking now and then.
Taste a single drop diluted in water. Infuse longer for more heat.
Strain through a coffee filter into dropper bottles and label clearly.

name: Vanilla Tincture
description: Split vanilla pods steeped in vodka for about two weeks. A few dashes add vanilla aroma without the sweetness of a syrup or liqueur.
storage: Room temperature, dropper bottle, away from light

steps.body: Split the vanilla pods lengthways, chop them and put them in a clean jar with the vodka.
Seal and infuse at room temperature for about 14 days, shaking every day or two.
Strain through a coffee filter into dropper bottles and label.

name: Cinnamon Tincture
description: Broken cinnamon sticks steeped in vodka for several days. Dashed or sprayed over drinks for a dry, woody spice note.
storage: Room temperature, dropper bottle, away from light

steps.body: Break up the cinnamon sticks and put them in a clean jar with the vodka.
Seal and infuse at room temperature for 5 days, shaking daily. Taste from day 3; it turns woody and astringent if left too long.
Strain through a coffee filter into dropper or atomiser bottles and label.

name: Sour Mix
description: Fresh lemon and lime juice blended with an equal measure of simple syrup. A ready sweet and sour base for high volume sours, margaritas and collinses.

steps.body: Juice and fine strain the lemons and limes.
Combine the juices with the simple syrup and stir.
Bottle, label with the date and keep in the fridge. Best used within a day.

name: Piña Colada Mix
description: Pineapple juice, cream of coconut and a little lime juice, ready to blend or shake with rum. Use about 100 ml of mix per 60 ml of rum.
storage: Fridge, sealed bottle, shake before use

steps.body: Warm the tin of cream of coconut in hot water and stir until smooth.
Blend all the ingredients briefly until fully combined.
Bottle and keep in the fridge. Shake hard before each use as the coconut fat separates.

name: Coconut Cream Mix
description: Three parts sweetened cream of coconut loosened with one part coconut milk. Pours easily from a bottle and stays smooth when shaken or blended in tiki drinks.
storage: Fridge, squeeze bottle, shake before use

steps.body: Warm the tins in hot water so the coconut fat softens, then empty them into a blender or jug.
Blend or whisk until completely smooth.
Pour into squeeze bottles and keep in the fridge. Let it warm slightly and shake before service.

name: Cold Brew Concentrate
description: Coarsely ground coffee steeped in cold water for 16 hours at a 1:4 ratio and filtered. Smooth and low in bitterness; used in coffee cocktails or diluted to drink.

steps.body: Put the ground coffee in a clean container, add the cold water and stir so all the grounds are wet.
Cover and steep in the fridge.
Strain through a fine sieve, then through a paper coffee filter.
Bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: House Ginger Beer
description: Fresh ginger juice, lemon juice, sugar and water, chilled and force carbonated. Spicier and drier than most bottled ginger beers; for Mules.

recipe.note: washed, juiced and fine strained, about 100 ml juice

steps.body: Juice the ginger and strain it through a fine cloth so no fibre is left to block the carbonator.
Stir the sugar into the water until dissolved, then add the ginger and lemon juices.
Chill the mix until very cold, close to 0 C. Cold liquid holds more gas.
Carbonate in a soda siphon or carbonation rig following the maker's instructions.
Keep sealed and cold. Use within three days.

name: Tepache
description: A Mexican drink of pineapple rind fermented for two to three days with piloncillo and cinnamon. Lightly fizzy, tangy and usually under 2 percent alcohol.

recipe.note: rind and core of 1 ripe pineapple, rinsed, not scrubbed

storage: Fridge, bottle with lid loose to vent gas

steps.body: Dissolve the piloncillo in the water in a clean, sanitised jar. Add the pineapple rind and core, cinnamon and cloves.
Cover with a cloth and leave at room temperature for 2 to 3 days. Skim off any white foam each day.
Taste daily. It is ready when lightly fizzy, sweet and tangy. Throw it away if it grows fuzzy mould or smells unpleasant.
Strain through a fine cloth, bottle and refrigerate. It keeps fermenting slowly, so leave the lid loose or vent the bottle daily.

name: Horchata
description: A Mexican rice drink made by soaking rice and cinnamon in water, blending, straining and sweetening. Milky and lightly spiced; used with rum and coffee.
storage: Fridge, sealed bottle, shake before use

steps.body: Rinse the rice, then soak it with the cinnamon in the water, covered, in the fridge.
Blend the rice, cinnamon and soaking water until very smooth.
Strain through a fine cloth or nut milk bag, squeezing well.
Stir in the sugar and vanilla until dissolved. Bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Hot Buttered Rum Batter
description: Softened butter creamed with brown sugar and ground winter spices. Put a heaped tablespoon in a mug with rum and top with hot water.

steps.body: Let the butter soften at room temperature.
Beat the butter with the sugar, spices, vanilla and salt until smooth and evenly mixed.
Pack into a tub or roll into a log in baking paper, and keep in the fridge.
To serve, stir about 25 g of batter with 50 ml of aged rum and 120 ml of hot water.

name: Tom and Jerry Batter
description: A thick, spiced batter of whipped egg whites folded into yolks beaten with sugar. Spooned into a mug with rum and brandy and topped with hot milk.

steps.body: Separate the eggs. Whisk the whites in a clean bowl to stiff peaks.
In another bowl, beat the yolks with the sugar, rum, vanilla and spices until thick and pale.
Fold the whites gently into the yolk mixture until even.
Keep chilled and use the same day. Contains raw egg; tell guests.
To serve, put 60 ml of batter in a warm mug with 30 ml rum and 30 ml brandy, then top with hot milk while stirring.

name: Eggnog Base
description: Eggs blended with sugar, milk, cream and nutmeg, without spirits. Add brandy, rum or bourbon per serve, or serve it plain as a non-alcoholic nog.
storage: Fridge, sealed bottle, shake before use

steps.body: Blend the eggs on low speed until smooth.
With the blender running, add the sugar slowly and blend until dissolved.
Add the nutmeg, milk and cream and blend just until combined.
Bottle and chill thoroughly before serving. Contains raw egg; keep cold, use within two days and tell guests.

name: Lightly Whipped Cream
description: Cold cream whipped only until it thickens but still pours. Floated over the back of a spoon onto an Irish Coffee so it sits on top.
storage: Fridge, sealed container; re-shake before use

steps.body: Pour the cold cream into a shaker tin, squeeze bottle or bowl.
Shake or whisk until it thickens to the texture of pouring yoghurt. It should ribbon off a spoon, not hold peaks.
Keep cold. Pour slowly over the back of a warm spoon to float it on the drink.

name: Chilli-Infused Tequila
description: Blanco tequila briefly infused with fresh red chillies. Gives clean, sharp heat to spicy margaritas and palomas.

recipe.note: fresh red, such as bird's eye, halved lengthways

steps.body: Wearing gloves, halve the chillies and add them to the tequila in a clean jar.
Infuse at room temperature, tasting every 5 minutes. Fresh chilli infuses fast.
Strain through a fine sieve as soon as the heat is where you want it.
Bottle and label. If it is too hot, blend it back with plain tequila.

name: Jalapeño-Infused Tequila
description: Blanco tequila infused for about 20 minutes with sliced jalapeño. Adds green, vegetal chilli flavour and moderate heat to margaritas.

steps.body: Slice the jalapeños and add them, seeds and all, to the tequila in a clean jar.
Infuse at room temperature, tasting often. Heat varies a lot from one jalapeño to the next.
Strain through a fine sieve once it is spicy enough.
Bottle and label.

name: Earl Grey-Infused Gin
description: Gin infused with loose Earl Grey tea for two hours. The tea adds bergamot and tannin; it is the base of the Earl Grey MarTEAni.

steps.body: Add the loose tea to the gin in a clean jar or the bottle, seal and shake.
Infuse at room temperature.
Strain through a fine sieve and then a coffee filter. Do not squeeze the leaves.
Bottle and label.

name: Butterfly Pea Gin
description: Gin infused with dried butterfly pea flowers until deep blue. The colour shifts to purple and pink when citrus or tonic is added.

steps.body: Add the dried flowers to the gin in a clean jar or the bottle, seal and shake.
Infuse at room temperature until the gin is deep blue.
Strain through a fine sieve or coffee filter.
Bottle, label and store away from sunlight, which fades the colour.

name: Strawberry-Infused Campari
description: Campari infused with fresh strawberries for a day or two. Softens the bitterness and adds ripe berry flavour to Negronis and spritzes.

steps.body: Combine the sliced strawberries and Campari in a clean jar and seal.
Infuse in the fridge for 24 to 48 hours, shaking once or twice.
Strain through a fine sieve, then a coffee filter, without pressing the fruit.
Bottle, label and keep in the fridge.

name: Pineapple-Infused Rum
description: Rum infused with ripe pineapple for several days and strained. A house take on pineapple rum for daiquiris, Old Fashioneds and tiki drinks.

recipe.note: or white rum for a lighter style
ripe, peeled and cut into chunks

steps.body: Combine the pineapple and rum in a clean jar and seal.
Infuse in the fridge for 3 to 5 days, shaking daily. Taste from day 3.
Strain through a fine sieve, then a coffee filter, pressing the fruit lightly.
Bottle, label and keep in the fridge.

name: Coconut Fat-Washed Rum
description: Rum mixed with melted coconut oil, frozen and strained so the fat is removed. Leaves a rich coconut aroma and a rounder texture.

steps.body: Melt the coconut oil gently and pour it into a wide container with the rum. Stir or shake well.
Leave at room temperature, shaking now and then.
Freeze until the fat has set into a solid layer.
Lift off or pierce the fat cap and strain the cold rum through a coffee filter. Bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Brown Butter-Washed Bourbon
description: Bourbon mixed with nutty browned butter, frozen and strained clear. Adds toasted, caramel and biscuit notes to Old Fashioneds and Manhattans.

steps.body: Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat and cook, swirling, until the milk solids turn golden brown and it smells nutty. Take off the heat at once.
Let the butter cool for a few minutes, then combine it with the bourbon in a wide container and stir well.
Leave at room temperature, stirring now and then.
Freeze until the butter has set solid.
Strain the cold bourbon through a coffee filter. Bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Bacon Fat-Washed Bourbon
description: Bourbon infused with warm rendered bacon fat, then frozen and strained. Smoky and savoury; the base of the Benton's Old Fashioned.

recipe.note: rendered from smoked bacon, strained, warm and liquid

steps.body: Cook smoked bacon and strain the rendered fat. Weigh out the warm, liquid fat.
Combine the fat and bourbon in a wide container and stir. Leave at room temperature.
Freeze until the fat has set solid.
Remove the fat and strain the cold bourbon through a coffee filter. Bottle, label as containing pork and keep in the fridge.

name: Olive Oil-Washed Gin
description: Gin shaken with extra virgin olive oil, frozen and strained. Gives Martinis a silky texture and a green, peppery olive note.

steps.body: Combine the gin and olive oil in a wide container, seal and shake hard.
Leave at room temperature, shaking now and then.
Freeze until the oil has set into a firm layer.
Working quickly while it is still frozen, strain the gin through a coffee filter. Bottle and keep in the fridge.

name: Coffee-Infused Campari
description: Campari infused with whole roasted coffee beans for a day. Adds roast and cocoa notes to Negronis, Boulevardiers and spritzes.

steps.body: Add the whole coffee beans to the Campari in a clean jar or the bottle and seal.
Infuse at room temperature. Taste after 12 hours and strain early if the coffee is strong enough.
Strain through a fine sieve.
Bottle and label.

name: Chamomile-Infused Bourbon
description: Bourbon infused with dried chamomile flowers for about 90 minutes. Adds a soft floral, apple and honey note to sours and Old Fashioneds.

steps.body: Add the chamomile to the bourbon in a clean jar, seal and shake.
Infuse at room temperature, shaking now and then.
Strain through a fine sieve and then a coffee filter, pressing the flowers lightly.
Bottle and label.

name: Cacao Nib-Infused Campari
description: Campari infused with roasted cacao nibs for a few hours. Adds dark chocolate depth to Negronis and Boulevardiers without any sweetness.

steps.body: Add the cacao nibs to the Campari in a clean jar, seal and shake.
Infuse at room temperature, shaking now and then. Taste and leave longer for a stronger chocolate note.
Strain through a fine sieve and then a coffee filter.
Bottle and label.

name: Banana-Infused Rum
description: Aged rum infused with ripe banana for a day and filtered. Gives natural banana flavour to daiquiris, Old Fashioneds and tiki drinks.

recipe.note: ripe with brown spots, peeled and sliced

steps.body: Combine the sliced banana and rum in a clean jar and seal.
Infuse in the fridge for 24 hours, shaking once or twice.
Strain through a fine sieve, then a coffee filter, without pressing the fruit.
Bottle, label and keep in the fridge.

name: Vanilla-Infused Vodka
description: Vodka infused with split vanilla pods for several days. A house vanilla vodka for Porn Star Martinis and Espresso Martinis.

steps.body: Split the vanilla pods lengthways and drop them into the vodka.
Seal and infuse at room temperature for 3 to 5 days, shaking daily.
Strain through a fine sieve once the flavour is full, then bottle and label.

name: Cucumber-Infused Gin
description: Gin infused with sliced cucumber overnight. Cool and green; used in Martinis, gin and tonics and summer coolers.

recipe.note: washed and thinly sliced, skin on

steps.body: Combine the sliced cucumber and gin in a clean jar and seal.
Infuse in the fridge.
Strain through a fine sieve and then a coffee filter, without pressing the cucumber.
Bottle, label and keep in the fridge.

name: Tea-Infused Vermouth
description: Sweet vermouth briefly infused with loose black tea. Adds tannin and a dry, malty note to Manhattans, Negronis and highballs.

recipe.note: loose leaf; Earl Grey or chai blends also work

steps.body: Add the loose tea to the vermouth in a clean jar, seal and shake.
Infuse at room temperature. Taste at 20 minutes; too long makes it bitter.
Strain through a fine sieve and then a coffee filter, without squeezing the leaves.
Bottle, label and keep in the fridge like any opened vermouth.

name: Salt Air
description: A light, salty lime foam made by blending water, lime juice, salt and soy lecithin. Spooned on top of a Margarita in place of a salt rim.
storage: Fridge, sealed container; re-blend to foam

steps.body: Combine the water, lime juice, salt and lecithin in a wide, deep container and stir until the salt has dissolved.
Tilt the container and run a stick blender just at the surface to pull in air until a thick layer of foam builds up.
Let the foam settle for a minute so it firms up, then spoon it onto the drink.
Blend again to make more foam as needed during service.

name: Citrus Foam
description: A sweet and sour lemon foam made with egg white and dispensed from a cream whipper. Aquafaba can replace the egg white for a vegan version.

recipe.note: about 4 whites, pasteurised; or the same volume of aquafaba

steps.body: Whisk the egg white, lemon juice, syrup and water together lightly, just to combine.
Fine strain into a 500 ml cream whipper so nothing blocks the nozzle. Do not fill past the maximum line.
Seal, charge with one nitrous oxide (N2O) cartridge and shake hard. Add a second charge if the foam is loose.
Chill for at least an hour before use.
Shake, hold upside down and dispense onto the drink. Keep in the fridge, use within a day and tell guests it contains egg.
